title: Where Did the Wires Go? PCB Explained Simply | PUC Electronics
description:
Aarav opens an old remote control and expects a nest of wires. Instead he finds a flat green board covered in thin copper lines. Where did all the wires go? In this animated lesson we open up printed circuit boards (PCBs).

First we build a PCB layer by layer: the insulating board, copper tracks, pads, the green solder mask and the white silkscreen. We compare single sided, double sided (with vias) and multilayer boards, and watch a simple PCB being made: copper clad board, layout printed in ink, etching in ferric chloride, cleaning, drilling and soldering. On a live breadboard two amperes flow through a 10 cm copper track while the readout and an oscilloscope show how much voltage a thin track loses compared with a wide one, using R = ρL / (w t). We list five advantages of PCBs, then a worked example finds the resistance of a real-size track, followed by the exam trap (A is the cross section, not the top area), where it is asked, an original JEE Main pattern practice question with a full solution, and a fact card to screenshot.

This is Episode 61 of PUC Electronics, Class 11, Chapter 9: Practical Electronic Components, their Specifications and PCB (Karnataka I PUC Electronics). It is the last episode of Class 11.
